soldier: Head orange-yellow or brownish yellow; the first and second antennal segments concolorous, while about three-quarters of the base of each segment from the third onwards is brown and the remainder pale yellow, the alternating light and dark forming rings, from which the species name is derived. Thorax, abdomen and legs yellow. Head with sparse fine setae mixed with a few long ones: one pair of long setae on the frons, one pair on the clypeus, one pair of apical setae and one pair of subapical setae on the labrum, four to five bristles on each side, and four long setae on each lateral margin of the anterior part of the postmentum. Head pear-shaped, very narrow near the mandibular bases, the posterior margin arched in a circular curve, the frons flat. Labrum elongate-lingulate, reaching the left marginal tooth, its apex rounded and blunt. Mandibles slender and straight, the apices gradually incurved; the left marginal tooth at one-third from the anterior end, its apex directed slightly forwards; the right mandible with an indistinct small tooth at a level below the left marginal tooth. Antennae usually with 16 segments, segment 4 the shortest, segments 2 and 3 almost equal, segment 3 one and a half times segment 4. Postmentum short, less than one and a half times as long as wide. Pronotum rhomboidal, the anterior margin with a rather deep median concavity, the posterior margin with a shallower median notch.
